ai.title: CLI analytics event tracking
ai.summary: Implemented comprehensive analytics event tracking in CLI. New `cli/src/utils/analytics.ts` module sends events to PostHog. Tracks slash menu activation, command usage, terminal completion, user input, knowledge file updates, and auth states. Update failures in `cli/release/index.js` now report to PostHog.

eli5.text: The command line app now quietly records which commands you run, when you open the autocomplete menu, and when it can't download an update, sending that information to a service called PostHog. If you use the command line tool, you won't see any new buttons or settings, but the app may now make a brief background internet connection when it launches or fails to update. These usage details are shared with the company to help the team understand how the tool gets used; the only way to notice it is to watch your network traffic or see the small update-check error messages that now also get logged remotely.

ai.title: Add DEBUGANALYTICS flag and expand analytics event properties
ai.summary: Introduces centralized `DEBUG_ANALYTICS` flag in `common/src/env.ts` to control dev-mode analytics logging via structured logger. Replaces local `DEBUG_DEV_EVENTS` in `cli/src/utils/analytics.ts` and applies to `common/src/analytics.ts`. Expands telemetry payloads: `router.ts` adds `durationMs`, `stdoutLength`, `mentionCount` to command/input events; `init.ts` adds `fileSizeBytes`; `index.tsx` masks paths with `isGitRepo`/`pathDepth`; `billing` adds token/latency details. Scope covers CLI core, shared env, agent runtime, and billing packages.

eli5.text: When you use commands in the assistant, it now collects more details about how each command runs, like how long it takes, how much text it returns, and whether it found what you asked for - and it does this without sending any of your private file paths. These details are turned on for developers building the assistant through a simple on/off switch, so they can see exactly what's being tracked while working on it, instead of having to dig through scattered settings in different places.

ai.summary: Bumped @opentui/core and @opentui/react to ^0.1.70 in cli/package.json. Documented bracketed paste mode necessity in cli/knowledge.md to resolve tmux send-keys partial input issues caused by async event processing timing.

eli5.text: When you paste text into the command-line tool (like pasting a multi-line message), the tool now correctly receives the entire pasted content instead of cutting off partway through. Previously, fast-paced pasted input would arrive in fragments, leaving you with only the last few characters in your message. The tool now recognizes paste operations and handles them as complete chunks, so multi-line or longer pastes land fully in your input field.

ai.title: Add card-based grid layout for implementor proposals
ai.summary: Implementor agent proposals now render in a responsive card grid via ImplementorGroup, replacing sequential list view. Logic in `cli/src/components/implementor-row.tsx` calculates columns based on terminal width (1 for xs/sm, 2 for md, 3 for lg) and distributes agents round-robin. `message-block.tsx` groups consecutive implementor agents using `groupConsecutiveImplementors` before rendering. Status indicators unified via new `getAgentStatusInfo` helper in `cli/src/utils/agent-helpers.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant shows you several implementation proposals side by side in the message log, they now appear as a responsive grid of cards instead of a single vertical list, so you can compare file stats, inline diffs, and status of each agent at a glance. As you resize the terminal, the grid automatically adjusts from one card per row on narrow windows up to three cards per row on wider ones, distributing the agents across columns for balanced reading.

ai.title: Fix MCP tool execution for subagents
ai.summary: Subagent MCP tool calls now execute correctly. The `MCPConfig` type moved `headers` from stdio to http/sse variants. `sdk/src/run.ts` adds explicit `callMCPTool` handling for `action.mcpConfig`. Covers `.agents`, `agents`, and `common` templates.

eli5.text: When you ask a helper agent to run a task that itself needs to use MCP tools (smaller plugins that extend its abilities), those tool calls now actually run instead of failing silently. The configuration that controls how the helper connects to external services no longer allows custom HTTP headers on local-only (stdio) plugins, those headers are now only permitted on remote plugins that connect over HTTP or SSE. The engine that drives subagents now includes an explicit step to execute an MCP tool when the task configuration says one is available, so if you look at what your agents are doing you will see them successfully invoking the tools you intended. The fix is live today across standard agent project templates.

ai.title: Fix analytics logger init cycle in CLI
ai.summary: Removed `logger` import from `cli/src/utils/analytics.ts` to break a circular dependency during initialization. Replaced `logger.debug` calls with a local `logAnalyticsDebug` helper using `console.debug` guarded by `DEBUG_ANALYTICS`. Scope limited to CLI analytics utilities. Helper silently catches console errors in restricted environments.

eli5.text: When the assistant quietly watches how people use it to learn from mistakes, it used to set off a startup snag where two parts waited on each other before either was ready. Now that logging step starts up on its own without tripping over the analytics system during launch. This makes the startup sequence smoother and prevents the tool from hanging or erroring out when it first opens. The change is live today and affects everyone who runs the assistant from the command line.

ai.title: Lazy-load logger for analytics debug
ai.summary: cli/src/utils/analytics.ts lazy-loads logger module for debug messages. Caches logger import promise to avoid repeated module resolution. Falls back to console.debug if logger import fails. Applies to CLI analytics debug output.

eli5.text: When you turn on analytics debugging in the command-line tool, it now waits to load its detailed logging helper only at the moment a debug message is actually needed, rather than loading it upfront. The CLI still shows the same debug output to you; the difference is that, if loading that logging helper fails for any reason, it simply falls back to the standard debug output instead of breaking. This only affects debug-time analytics messages from the command-line tool and is already live today.

ai.title: CLI version bump to 1.0.579
ai.summary: The CLI package manifest at `cli/release/package.json` is updated from 1.0.578 to 1.0.579, the version shipped in this release-bump commit. This version bundles the same-day CLI improvements: box-drawing Unicode markdown tables, pause/resume timer behavior during ask_user, multi-byte IME input support, static fs/path imports, opentui 0.1.70 upgrade, card-based implementor proposal grid, and expanded analytics event tracking with DEBUG_ANALYTICS and payload properties. The change is a pure manifest increment gating distribution of the accumulated CLI core, agent-runtime, billing, and knowledge-file changes noted in the release window.
ai.evidence: Diff hunk in `cli/release/package.json` bumps the `version` field from `1.0.578` to `1.0.579`; metadata indicates a release-bump commit with stats +1 / -1.

eli5.text: This release brings smarter table rendering, better multilingual typing support, and improved analytics tracking to the Freebuff CLI. Tables in your terminal now display with clean Unicode borders that adjust proportionally to fit your screen width, making data easier to read. Chinese, Japanese, and Korean users can now type naturally in multiline input fields without characters being dropped, since the input system properly handles multi-byte text. The status bar timer now pauses when the CLI asks you a question, so you get an accurate reading of conversation time instead of elapsed wall-clock time while waiting for your response. Agent proposals now appear in a responsive card layout that adapts from one column on narrow screens to three columns on wider terminals, replacing the old vertical list with a more scannable grid view. Internal analytics improvements help capture richer usage data for product insights, with debugging capabilities available for developers through a new centralized flag. Upgrading gives you cleaner tables, reliable international typing, accurate timing, and a more organized view of AI agent suggestions in your terminal.

ai.title: MCP env vars support $VARNAME syntax
ai.summary: Agent definitions now accept `$VAR_NAME` strings in MCP server `env` blocks, resolving them from `process.env` at load time via `resolveMcpEnv` in `sdk/src/agents/load-agents.ts`. This replaces hardcoded tokens (e.g., `ntn_***`) with secure references (e.g., `$NOTION_TOKEN`) in `.agents/notion-agent.ts` and `.agents/notion-researcher.ts`. Missing variables throw errors during `loadLocalAgents`, skipping the agent if `verbose` logging is enabled. Type definitions in `util-types.ts` document the behavior across core, agents, and template directories.

eli5.text: Starting today, you can stop pasting your private app tokens (like your Notion API key) directly into your agent configuration files. Instead, you can write a placeholder like `$NOTION_TOKEN` and the system will automatically fill in the real token from your computer's environment variables when it loads the agent. This keeps your secret keys out of shared or version-controlled files, so you can store them safely in a separate environment file. If a referenced token is missing, the agent will stop and tell you about it rather than silently failing.

ai.title: Ad banner fallback for missing title
ai.summary: Ad banner CTA text now defaults to 'Learn more' when ad.title is empty. Ad impression inserts coerce null title and favicon fields to empty strings. Covers cli/src/components/ad-banner.tsx and web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts. Prevents undefined rendering and satisfies non-null column constraints.

eli5.text: When an ad that's shown to you has no headline, it now displays 'Learn more' instead of leaving a blank space. Behind the scenes, the system also converts any missing subtitle and logo fields into empty text before saving a record of the ad being shown, so nothing breaks when those details are absent. If you happen to notice an ad without a title, the call-to-action button will simply read 'Learn more'. This change is live today for the CLI tool's ad banner display.

eli5.text: When an AI helper makes a tiny, obvious fix (like changing one line), it now skips running its full battery of checks and only runs the quick, relevant ones, so you don't wait around for unnecessary busywork. Also, after it finishes helping you, it will now suggest your next steps or follow-up questions at the very end of its reply, instead of bringing them up in the middle of working through your request. This is live today for anyone using the assistant.

ai.title: Fallback to cta for ad title in API
ai.summary: The `postAds` function in `web/src/app/api/v1/ads/_post.ts` now uses `ad.cta` as a fallback when `ad.title` is empty, preventing blank titles in `adImpression` database records. This ensures ad impressions retain meaningful text even if the primary title field is missing.

eli5.text: When your system creates a record every time an ad is shown, it used to leave the title field blank if the ad didn't have a title. Now, if the ad has no title, it will automatically use the call-to-action text (like a button label) instead, so those records always have meaningful text. If you looked at the records your system stores for shown ads, you'd see this backup text in places where you previously saw nothing. This affects anyone looking at ad performance reports when ads lack titles.

eli5.text: When you set up an AI assistant that connects to external tools, the assistant can now read your computer's environment variables correctly even when those variables are configured dynamically. Previously, references like $MY_API_KEY in tool settings would sometimes fail to resolve; that lookup now works reliably for all such variable references. This only affects the part of the software that prepares these tool connections, so you'll notice it if you rely on environment-variable-based settings for your tools. This fix is live today.
